definitions.explanation: Help or assistance offered to someone in trouble or distress. Often used figuratively to describe timely aid that saves a dire situation.

examples.japanese: {救|すく}いの{手|て}を{差|さ}し{伸|の}べる。
{困|こま}っているときに{救|すく}いの{手|て}が{現|あらわ}れた。
examples.english: A helping hand appeared when I was in trouble.

examples.japanese: {被災者|ひさいしゃ}に{救|すく}いの{手|て}を{差|さ}し{伸|の}べるため、{多|おお}くのボランティアが{集|あつ}まった。
examples.english: Many volunteers gathered to lend a helping hand to the disaster victims.

notes:
{救|すく}いの{手|て} literally means "hand of rescue" and refers to timely help given to someone in trouble. It is often used figuratively and carries a somewhat dramatic or literary tone.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {救|すく}いの{手|て}を{差|さ}し{伸|の}べる: to extend a helping hand (the most common collocation)
- {救|すく}いの{手|て}を{求|もと}める: to seek a helping hand
- {救|すく}いの{手|て}が{現|あらわ}れる: a helping hand appears

USAGE:
Frequently appears in news reports about disaster relief, charitable aid, and personal crises. Also used in everyday speech to describe someone who helped at a critical moment.

RELATED WORDS:
- {手|て}を{貸|か}す: to lend a hand (more casual)
- {助|たす}け{舟|ぶね}: a lifeboat, timely help (similar figurative use)
- {援助|えんじょ}: aid, assistance (more formal/official)
